sections.content:
A Qatar work visa is an entry permit that allows a foreign national to enter Qatar for employment, and it is the first step in a two-stage process. After arrival, the entry visa must be converted into a Work Residence Permit, and the worker receives a Qatar ID, which is the operational document for daily life. Without a valid Qatar ID, a worker cannot open a bank account, sign a lease or access most government services.

The system is entirely employer-sponsored: you cannot apply independently. A Qatari employer with a valid commercial registration and an active establishment ID with the Ministry of Labour applies on your behalf through the Ministry of Interior. Since the 2020 labour reforms, workers can change employers after serving their notice period without a No Objection Certificate, but the new employer must still sponsor a fresh visa.
sections.title: How the Qatar Work Visa System Works

sections.content:
To qualify, you must be at least 18 years old, hold a passport valid for at least 6 months, and have a confirmed job offer with a signed employment contract from a licensed Qatari employer. For skilled and white-collar roles, educational certificates must be attested end to end: state attestation, the foreign ministry of your home country, the Qatar embassy, and finally Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs after arrival. The full attestation chain can take 3 to 6 weeks.

Other requirements include a medical fitness examination, usually completed before departure at a Qatar Visa Center, biometric capture, and a police clearance certificate attested by the Qatar embassy for many nationalities. The employer's side includes a trade license, establishment ID, immigration card and labour quota approval. A degree submitted without the full attestation chain can fail the employer's submission even after the offer is signed.
sections.title: Eligibility and Document Requirements

sections.content:
The standard sequence starts with the employer's visa application, followed by the worker's Qatar Visa Center appointment for contract signing, biometrics and medical checks. Once approved, an entry visa is issued, the worker flies to Qatar, and the employer finalizes the Qatar ID within 30 days of arrival. The full journey typically takes 2 to 6 weeks, though peak hiring seasons and QVC slot availability can extend it.

Costs are modest compared with other Gulf states: the company-sponsored work visa fee is around QAR 200 to 300, plus a Qatar ID fee of about QAR 330 and medical costs. By law, employers cover most visa costs, but practices vary, so confirm in writing who pays each fee before signing. Beware of agents who demand large upfront payments without a verifiable employer, contract and visa reference number.
sections.title: Step-by-Step Process and Costs

sections.content:
Qatar's 2020 reforms, under Law No. 18 and Law No. 19, abolished the general No Objection Certificate requirement for changing jobs and removed exit-permit requirements for most workers. Workers can now move to a new employer after serving the contractual notice period and completing the Ministry of Labour transfer process, including a new medical examination. The reform also strengthened wage protection and minimum wage rules.

For workers already in Qatar, the transfer process requires the new employer's sponsorship, an attested labour contract and a fresh residence permit application. Workers should keep copies of every contract, payslip and visa document, since these are needed for transfers, family sponsorship and end-of-service claims. Family residence sponsorship generally requires a minimum salary threshold and an attested marriage certificate.
